svg.title: Compare zygote origin before making genetic claims
svg.desc: The dizygotic panel shows two separate zygotes, each from a separate fertilization, developing into two embryos. The monozygotic panel shows one zygote origin and one early embryo giving rise to two developing embryos. Similar symbolic embryo colors do not mean identical genomes or phenotypes. Dizygotic twins have a relationship broadly like other siblings of the same parents; monozygotic twins share much inherited genetic information but can differ through later mutations, gene expression and environment. Membranes are omitted; monozygotic twins do not universally share one placenta or chorion. The model makes no exact splitting-day rule.

g.text: Compare zygote origin before making genetic claims
The branching model depicts origins, not placental anatomy or an exact splitting timetable.
One early embryo gives rise to two
Shared origin does not require identical gene expression, environments or later mutations.
Monozygotic twins do not always share one chorion or placenta; membranes are not drawn here.
A photograph of two fetuses alone cannot establish every genetic relationship.
